articles.title: India Begins Identifying ‘AI-Proof’ Jobs to Protect Workers From Automation
articles.summary: Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal said he had directed his ministry to identify sectors where AI could improve productivity without necessarily replacing workers. Speaking to Indian students and researchers during an interaction in Berlin, Germany, Goyal highlighted India’s traditional strengths in handicrafts, handlooms, tourism and culinary skills as potential sources of employment in an AI-driven economy.

articles.title: Indian Railways Launches First Salt Container Train In Gujarat
articles.summary: Indian Railways has launched a specialised salt container train between Shivlakha Gati Shakti Cargo Terminal in Kutch and Mithapur, Gujarat. Inaugurated on September 15, the service uses lightweight stainless-steel containers designed to protect salt from rain and moisture, improve loading capacity, streamline handling and reduce transportation costs for the salt industry.

articles.title: We deeply apologise: Organisers break silence after Shilpa Rao's set is cut short
articles.summary: The organisers of the Bollywood Music Project (BMP) have apologised after singer Shilpa Rao’s performance at the festival’s 10th anniversary edition in Mumbai was abruptly cut short on October 24. Her microphone and electronic audio equipment were reportedly switched off mid-performance after the event ran behind schedule. The incident drew criticism from festival-goers and fans, and #JusticeForShilpaRao began trending online.

articles.title: Piyush Goyal flags India’s ‘AI-proof’ strengths, pushes tech, investment ties with Germany
articles.summary: Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal has highlighted India’s traditional strengths in an AI-driven world, saying that no amount of artificial intelligence can replace the country’s handicrafts, handloom, culinary skills and tourism. Speaking after engagements during his Germany visit, Goyal said India’s skilled workforce, youthful population and traditional expertise offer opportunities for global leadership.

articles.title: Ramayana movie advance booking: Nearly 2 lakh tickets sold in India; overseas numbers
articles.summary: Ramayana has collected ₹ 11. 38 crore through advance bookings across its first three days in India. Films Discourse reported these figures on 25 October at 5:43 AM. The film has sold 1,96,148 tickets across 12,604 shows in 151 cities nationwide. These numbers cover the first three days of the film’s opening, rather than opening day alone.

articles.title: Global Youth Protests Highlight Deepening Economic Discontent And Inequality
articles.summary: Young people across the world are staging protests over high unemployment, stagnant wages, and rising living costs. Movements in countries like Bangladesh, Nepal, India, and parts of Europe reflect a growing frustration with broken economic promises and stark inequality. Experts warn that governments must renew the social contract to restore trust and opportunity for future generations.

articles.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang says US regulation pushed China’s domestic capabilities
articles.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has said that export curbs and trade restrictions imposed by Washington have served as a ‘catalyst’ for China’s rapid progress in semiconductor development. Speaking to CNBC on the sidelines of Nvidia's GTC Berlin conference, Huang stated that American regulatory measures effectively pushed China to speed up its own domestic chip manufacturing and strive for technological self-reliance.

articles.title: Dalit Politics in Tamil Nadu Faces Ongoing Social Justice Challenges
articles.summary: Activist Shalin Maria Lawrence and politician D Ravikumar claim that despite decades of Dravidian party rule in Tamil Nadu, social justice remains elusive for Dalits. articles.title: Arshdeep Singh sets India record for most T20I wickets in a calendar year
articles.summary: India’s left-arm fast bowler Arshdeep Singh created history on Saturday, becoming India’s leading wicket-taker in men’s T20 Internationals in a calendar year during the second T20I against New Zealand at Hagley Oval in Christchurch. Arshdeep achieved the milestone after returning figures of 2 for 33, taking his wicket tally in 2026 to 38.
